question.worked_solution:
Since $f(15)=-4$ is $14$ jumps after $f(1),$ we can determine the first term of the sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(15) & =f(1)+14d \\ -4 & =f(1)+14(-5) \\ -4 & =f(1)-70 \\ 66 & =f(1)\end{aligned}
$$

So, the formula for the $n$th term is:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(n) & =f(1)+(n-1)d \\  & =66+(n-1)(-5) \\  & =66-5n+5 \\  & =71-5n\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for the value of $n$ that gives $f(n)=-184,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(n) & =71-5n \\ -184 & =71-5n \\ -255 & =-5n \\ n & =\frac{-255}{-5} \\ n & =51\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $-184$ is the $51$st term of the sequence.
